items.followUp: State Newton’s Second Law of Motion and use it to derive the relation between force, mass and acceleration.

rubric.why: States the essential relationship in Newton’s Second Law.
rubric.description: States that force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum, in the direction of the force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the proportionality between force and rate of change of momentum.

rubric.why: Uses the momentum relation needed in the proof.
rubric.description: Writes momentum as mass multiplied by velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying momentum as p = mv.

rubric.why: Shows that the rate of change of momentum becomes mass times acceleration for constant mass.
rubric.description: For constant mass, relates the rate of change of momentum to m(v − u)/t = ma.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct derivation to ma.

rubric.why: States the required result.
rubric.description: Obtains F = ma in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final relation.

modelAnswer: Newton’s Second Law states that the rate of change of momentum of a body is proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction of that force.
Momentum, p = mv.
For a body of constant mass m, rate of change of momentum = (mv − mu)/t = m(v − u)/t.
Since a = (v − u)/t, force is proportional to ma.
In SI units, the proportionality constant is 1; therefore, F = ma.

items.followUp: Define the addition of forces. Explain how the head-to-tail rule gives the resultant of two perpendicular forces.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of adding forces.
rubric.description: Defines addition of forces as combining forces to find their single resultant (vector sum).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining the resultant or vector sum of forces.

rubric.why: Checks the vector construction described by the rule.
rubric.description: Places the tail of the second force at the head of the first and draws the resultant from the first tail to the final head.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct head-to-tail construction.

rubric.why: Checks that the components are identified as perpendicular.
rubric.description: Shows or states that the two component forces meet at 90°.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for indicating the perpendicular relationship.

rubric.why: Checks the resultant interpretation or its magnitude/direction for perpendicular components.
rubric.description: Identifies the diagonal as the resultant, with magnitude √(Fx² + Fy²) (and direction tan θ = Fy/Fx).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the diagonal resultant or a correct magnitude/direction relation.

modelAnswer: Addition of forces is the vector addition of two or more forces to find their single resultant force.
For perpendicular components Fx and Fy, draw Fx and then draw Fy from the head of Fx, at 90° to it.
The resultant R is drawn from the tail of Fx to the head of Fy; it is the diagonal of the right-angled construction.
Its magnitude is R = √(Fx² + Fy²), and its direction is given by tan θ = Fy/Fx.

items.followUp: A pump lifts 50 kg of water through 12 m in 8 s. Calculate its power, taking g = 9.8 m s⁻².

rubric.why: Checks identification of the given quantities.
rubric.description: Identifies the water mass, height and time with their units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the relevant data.

rubric.why: Checks the appropriate power/work relation.
rubric.description: Uses P = W/t and W = mgh, or directly P = mgh/t.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Checks correct substitution and arithmetic, allowing the common approximation g = 10 m s⁻².
rubric.description: Substitutes the data and evaluates the power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution or calculated value.

rubric.why: Checks the final power and unit.
rubric.description: Gives approximately 1.10 kW (or 1097.6 W using g = 9.8 m s⁻²; 1120 W using g = 10 m s⁻²).
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a correct value with unit; award 1 if the value is correct but the unit is missing.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 70 kg; h = 16 m; t = 10 s; g = 9.8 m s⁻².
Formula: P = W/t and W = mgh, so P = mgh/t.
